assessment.model_case: The projected mean of about 1.55 shots sits above 1.5, so the under rests on a median of one and depends on the distribution's shape. His 16.2 projected minutes could rise if Calgary is short at center, and the low end of the sensitivity range barely clears break-even.
assessment.price_case: +130 on the main 1.5 line needs a win rate somewhat below even money. The minimum acceptable price is about +104 and model fair odds are near -121. Two other books price the under similarly, so this is a model-versus-market gap, not one stale book.
assessment.context_case: Calgary is missing multiple centers, and Frost's day-to-day status could reshape Sharangovich's deployment. BetOnline's settlement rules are assumed standard but have not been verified.
blocking_checks: Morgan Frost's status: if Frost sits with Huberdeau and Pospisil out, Sharangovich may gain minutes or power-play time. That would push shots further above a projection already over the line.

qualitative_review.countercase: Because the mean is above the line, modest role growth flips the case. The over lean at two other books may reflect expected usage. This bet is correlated with the Hughes under in the same game, so the two should not be treated as independent confirmations.

findings.note: NHL's game page ranks Seattle's penalty kill last in the league at 60.7%, while Edmonton's power play is second at 32.6%; Seattle also allows 3.55 goals per game (28th), and Kraken goalie Joey Daccord has a .872 save percentage.

McDavid leads the league with 59 points (14 goals, 45 assists) and has a point in all 13 home games this season, but that streak only means at least one point per game, not the two this bet needs; Edmonton has also lost four in a row.

The Oilers' preview says Babcock had no update on Zach Hyman (listed day-to-day elsewhere), Hallander is out for an extended period, and the team is rested after the break; it also shows Bouchard and Draisaitl among the top-four scorers and notes the Oilers play in Seattle the next night.
